text: **dsh-skills-symlink** 是 DSH 的 Web 插件：为每个项目单独配置可用的技能目录，并从分类目录中发现嵌套技能。它注册项目技能提供器，读取项目内的 `.dsh/skill-paths.yaml`，可按深度展开目录、监听配置与技能变化。设置页可查看和编辑项目路径，插件详情页展示各项目的技能分类与目录结构。适合按项目隔离技能集合、复用分类技能库的 DSH 用户；需要 Node.js 与兼容版本的 DSH，不需要额外 API 密钥。

**dsh-skills-symlink** adds project-specific skill folders and nested discovery to DSH Web. It reads each project’s `.dsh/skill-paths.yaml`, expands folders by depth, and watches changes. The settings tab edits paths; the plugin page shows skill categories. Requires DSH and Node.js; no API key.
按项目分别加载技能目录，别让所有项目共用一套。
让 DSH 从 category/skill/SKILL.md 这种多层目录里找到技能。
我想在插件设置页编辑项目的 skillPaths。
有没有办法看每个工作区实际加载了哪些技能？
新增技能后希望不用重启会话就能刷新目录。
同一个技能库能不能按项目挑选不同类别？
Load different skill folders for each DSH project.
Show me which skills and categories each workspace currently resolves.
**dsh-skills-symlink** 的功能「项目级技能路径」：每个项目在 `.dsh/skill-paths.yaml` 中列出自己的 `skillPaths`，提供器据此解析项目根目录并返回对应技能根目录。
**dsh-skills-symlink** 的功能「嵌套分类目录扫描」：配置 `maxDepth` 后，插件展开分类和分组目录，再调用 DSH 文件系统技能发现；还能忽略指定目录并限制展开根目录数量。
**dsh-skills-symlink** 的功能「配置与技能热更新」：启用监听后，项目配置文件变化会使技能缓存失效，技能根目录交由 DSH watcher 观察，从而反映目录增删。
**dsh-skills-symlink** 的功能「项目技能管理界面」：设置页读取工作区的路径并保存项目配置；插件详情页按工作区展示技能总数、分类组成和目录中的技能名称。
dsh-skills-symlink 使用前须知：该插件要求 DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.5` 和 Node.js `^22.19.0` 或 `>=24.0.0`；安装时还需按 README 所述访问 GitHub 获取包。
dsh-skills-symlink 使用前须知：技能路径写在项目的 `.dsh/skill-paths.yaml`；`maxDepth`、`ignore` 等插件选项要在 DSH profile 的插件行配置。

dsh-skills-symlink README · Introduction：Give every project in [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) its own set of skills. It replaces the skill symlink from Hermes: one shared library, and each project loads only the categories it lists. The plugin creates no symbolic links; the name only borrows the Hermes term.

dsh-skills-symlink README · ✨ Highlights：- 🗂️ **Per-project skill sets**: one `.dsh/skill-paths.yaml` per project, and each project sees only what it lists
- 📚 **One path for a categorised library**: `maxDepth` reads `category/skill/SKILL.md` layouts up to 6 levels deep
- 🔥 **Hot reload**: add or remove a skill without restarting DSH
- 🛡️ **Safe by default**: paths and symlinks outside the project are rejected, and the plugin makes no outbound requests
- 🩺 **Diagnostics built in**: a log of every root scanned, plus a post-install check script
- 🧭 **Visual overview**: see each project's skill mix on the Plugins page

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🤔 Why：If you came from Hermes, you will miss its skill symlink. A skill lives once in a central repository, and any project that wants it symlinks it into its own skills directory. Edit the original and every project follows, with nothing to copy. Project A links the three writing skills, project B links the two tools skills, and each sees exactly its own set. Adding a skill is one more link; nothing else changes.

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🤔 Why：DSH replaced that with skill roots configured through `customSkillDirs`. Three things break on the way over.

First, each root only accepts `<root>/<skill>/SKILL.md`. A library laid out as `category/skill/SKILL.md` yields nothing when you point at the parent, with no error and no log line.

Second, the setting belongs to the host or the preset, not to the project. Every project sees the same skills, and "this project sees category A only" cannot be expressed.

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🤔 Why：Third, every skill's name and description goes into context each turn. With a large library that cost is fixed and cannot be scoped down.

This plugin moves the paths into the project, one `.dsh/skill-paths.yaml` per project, and `maxDepth` in the plugin row lets it read category folders, so a single parent path is enough. From one library, project A loads 17 skills and project B loads 28.

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🤔 Why：


One library, two projects: A loads 17 skills, B loads 28.

dsh-skills-symlink README · 📦 Install：Requires DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0` (the 0.2.x line), Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`, and access to GitHub while installing.

**DSH Desktop:** open **Plugins** in the sidebar and add

```text
github:MYSTERY2019/dsh-skills-symlink#v0.4.0
```

Restart DSH afterwards; `dsh-skills-symlink` should appear on the Plugins page. The 0.2.x `dsh` CLI refuses `--profile desktop`, so Desktop installs from the Plugins page only.

**Other profiles (for example `web`) from the command line:**

dsh-skills-symlink README · 📦 Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:MYSTERY2019/dsh-skills-symlink#v0.4.0
```

You can also download `dsh-skills-symlink-0.4.0.tgz` from the Release and pass its path instead of the `github:...` spec.

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🚀 Use：Create `.dsh/skill-paths.yaml` in the project root:

```yaml
version: 1
skillPaths:
  - skills
  - tools/skills

The project now sees only the skills under those two directories. Other projects do not. Paths are relative to the project root (the nearest Git root, otherwise the session's working directory).

A shared library outside the project needs `allowExternalPaths` in the plugin row first (see Configuration). Without it, that entry is skipped and the log says why:

```yaml

dsh-skills-symlink README · needs allowExternalPaths: true in the plugin row：version: 1
skillPaths:
  - ../shared-skills
```

The project file knows two keys, `version` and `skillPaths`. Options such as `maxDepth` and `ignore` belong to the plugin row; written into the project file they have no effect. The plugin ignores them, logs where they belong, and still loads the paths. An invalid entry (outside the project, not a string) is skipped on its own as well.
section: needs allowExternalPaths: true in the plugin row

text:
dsh-skills-symlink README · One path for a categorised library：If the library is laid out as `category/skill/SKILL.md`, the project file still names the parent:

```yaml
version: 1
skillPaths:
  - skills
```

and `maxDepth` in the plugin row says how deep to go (see Configuration):

| Layout | `maxDepth` |
|---|--:|
| `root/skill/SKILL.md` | 1 (default) |
| `root/category/skill/SKILL.md` | 2 |
| `root/group/category/skill/SKILL.md` | 3 |

Valid values are 1 to 6. Anything else (`0`, `7`, `2.5`) is treated as 1, with a warning in the plugin log.
section: One path for a categorised library

text:
dsh-skills-symlink README · When you add a skill later：| Where you put it | What happens | Work needed |
|---|---|---|
| Inside a category you already list, as `category/new-skill/SKILL.md` | picked up like its neighbours | none |
| As a new sub-category, `category/new-group/skill/SKILL.md` | promoted to its own root | none, if `maxDepth` already reaches that depth |
| As a new top-level category beside the ones you list | invisible, because the project file names categories one by one | add a line per project, or list the common parent instead |
| Deeper than `maxDepth` allows | invisible, and that root reports 0 skills | raise `maxDepth` in the plugin row |

text:
dsh-skills-symlink README · When you add a skill later：Skills are read when a session starts, so a change appears in the next session rather than the one
that is running. `scripts/post-install-check.mjs` points at the depth case when a root resolves to
zero skills but holds `SKILL.md` files one level further down.

text:
dsh-skills-symlink README · ✅ Check that it took effect：After installing and restarting, run the check that ships with the package:

```bash
node ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-skills-symlink/scripts/post-install-check.mjs --project .
```

dsh-skills-symlink README · ✅ Check that it took effect：It prints the profile that holds the plugin, the version the host actually loaded, and every root
your project resolves. A version mismatch, a missing plugin row, or a project without a config
file is listed as a problem and the exit code becomes 1. Pass `--profile` to look at another
profile, or `--json` to script it.

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🔧 Configuration：Override the plugin row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: dsh-skills-symlink
  config:
    maxDepth: 2
    allowExternalPaths: true

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🔧 Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `maxDepth` | `1` | How many levels to scan, an integer from 1 to 6 |
| `ignore` | `[]` | Category or group folder names skipped while descending; `prefix*` is supported; case-insensitive on Windows |
| `maxRoots` | `2000` | Most roots one project may expand into. Configured roots always stay, the rest of the budget is shared fairly between them, and empty folders watched only for new skills do not count |
| `allowExternalPaths` | `false` | Allow absolute paths, `..`, and symbolic links that point outside the project |
| `watch` | `true` | Watch skill folders so adding or removing a skill needs no restart |
| `watchFollowSymlinks` | same as `allowExternalPaths` | Whether watching follows symbolic links |
| `configWatchIntervalMs` | `500` | How often `.dsh/skill-paths.yaml` is checked, 10–60000 ms |
| `diagnosticsFile` | `true` | Write the diagnostics log |
| `logFile` | `''` | Custom log path; a relative path is resolved from the profile directory; empty writes `<profile>/logs/dsh-skills-symlink.log` |

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🔧 Configuration：A number that is out of range or not an integer falls back to its default with a warning; it never stops DSH from starting.

> [!WARNING]
> When DSH overrides a plugin row it replaces `config` as a whole; it does not merge. Write every key you need in one block, or the rest falls back to defaults. A row with only `maxDepth`, for example, turns `allowExternalPaths` back to `false`, and paths outside the project are skipped (and logged).

Skills overview on the Plugins page: one row per project, expanded to its skill mix and folder tree.

text:
dsh-skills-symlink README · 🩺 Troubleshooting：The first time skills are listed in a project, the plugin writes a block to `<profile>/logs/dsh-skills-symlink.log`:

```text
roots() first call for cwd=.../my-app: projectRoot=.../my-app, configFile=found,
  configuredRoots=2, roots=3, watchOnlyRoots=1, maxDepth=2
  root[0] .../my-app/skills/web
  root[1] .../my-app/skills/data

Each `root[i]` is a folder this project actually scanned. When a skill is missing, start from this list.

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🩺 Troubleshooting：Common causes: `maxDepth` too small, the folder matched by `ignore`, a path outside the project (or a symbolic link pointing outside it) without `allowExternalPaths`, or plugin options written into the project file. The last three each leave a warning in the log.

A successful load writes an `applied` line. `no project config at ...` means the project has no config file.

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🏆 Which skill wins on a name clash：The lower rank wins:

| Source | rank |
|---|--:|
| `<project>/.dsh/skills` | 100 |
| `<project>/.agents/skills` | 200 |
| Roots configured by this plugin | 250 |
| Global `customSkillDirs` | 300 |
| User-level folders | 400 / 500 |

Between this plugin's own roots, the order is depth (shallower first), then `skillPaths` order, then code-point order of folder names (`B` sorts before `a`).
section: 🏆 Which skill wins on a name clash

text: dsh-skills-symlink README · 🏆 Which skill wins on a name clash：Every shadowed copy is logged with the `SKILL.md` paths of both sides, at `maxDepth: 1` too, and again when the set of clashes changes.
section: 🏆 Which skill wins on a name clash

text: dsh-skills-symlink README · 🔒 Security：The plugin reads files only while DSH resolves skills, and writes only the selected workspace's `.dsh/skill-paths.yaml` when you save the settings card. It makes no outbound requests and reads no credentials.

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🔒 Security：- Absolute paths and `..` are rejected by default. Whether a path is inside the project is decided by its real path, so a symbolic link inside the project that points outside is rejected too, and checked again when a skill's body is loaded. Cloning someone else's repository cannot make DSH read other files on your machine.
- Writes go only to workspaces DSH knows, are refused when the `.dsh` folder or the config file is a symbolic link, and go through a temporary file and a rename, so a half-written file is never left behind.
- A write request must be same-origin, `application/json`, and at most 16 KB.

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🔀 Differences from upstream：This repository is a fork of [NeoRrrr/dsh-project-skill-paths](https://github.com/NeoRrrr/dsh-project-skill-paths) v0.3.0.

| | upstream v0.3.0 | here v0.4.0 |
|---|:--:|:--:|
| Per-project `skillPaths` | ✅ | ✅ |
| Settings card | ✅ | ✅ |
| Hot reload | ✅ | ✅ |
| Multi-level scan `maxDepth` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `ignore` / `maxRoots` | ❌ | ✅ |
| Fake-skill guard | ❌ | ✅ |
| Loads on DSH 0.2.x | ❌ | ✅ |

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🔀 Differences from upstream：The repository, the package name and the plugin id are all `dsh-skills-symlink`; that id is what the Plugins page shows. It does the same job as `dsh-project-skill-paths`; do not install both.

<details>
<summary>Expansion rules (edge cases)</summary>

dsh-skills-symlink README · 🔀 Differences from upstream：- **Descending and promoting are separate.** Every folder down to depth `maxDepth − 1` is visited, but only a folder whose direct children include a skill folder becomes a root. Pure grouping folders are walked through, so `maxDepth: 3` works for a grouped layout.
- **Expanded roots only count folder skills.** In a promoted category, top-level `.md` files are documentation and are dropped, so they never become fake skills. Flat `.md` skills placed directly in a configured root still work as upstream.
- **A folder holding only flat `.md` files is not promoted.** Put each skill in `<skill>/SKILL.md`, or add that folder itself to `skillPaths`.
- **No duplicates.** A folder with its own `SKILL.md` is a skill: it is never promoted and never descended into. Folders are de-duplicated by real path, so a symlinked alias adds nothing.
- **Hot reload.** With `watch: true` (the default) and `maxDepth ≥ 2`, empty category and group folders are watched too, so the first skill dropped in is found. These are the **Watched only** folders on the settings card; they do not count toward `maxRoots`.
- **One unreadable root only drops itself.** The
